title: Khoresh Bademjan
subtitle: aubergine stew
excerpt: Khoresh Bademjan is a Persian stew of tender lamb and fried aubergine cooked in a spiced tomato sauce with saffron. The aubergine absorbs all the surrounding flavour and becomes silky and rich. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Khoresh Bademjan is a staple of the Persian table, especially popular in summer when aubergines are at their best. The saffron and cinnamon combination is characteristic of Iranian cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 2 months. The aubergine softens further on reheating.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Persian word for a slow-cooked stew, always served over a mound of rice at the Iranian table.
The Persian word for aubergine, one of the most loved vegetables in Iranian cooking.

content.text: fried until golden before being braised with lamb, tomatoes and saffron. Frying the aubergine first is the key step. It seals the flesh and stops it turning to mush during the long cook. Serves 4.
The stew needs at least 90 minutes of slow simmering. The lamb should be falling-apart tender before the dish is done.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine rounds in batches for 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Set aside on kitchen paper.
In the dutch oven, heat the remaining oil over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, turning to colour all sides. Remove and set aside. Add more oil if the pot looks dry.
Fry the onions in the dutch oven over medium heat for 12 minutes until soft and golden. Add turmeric and cinnamon, stir for 1 minute. Return the lamb to the pot.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, saffron water and lemon juice. Stir to combine. Bring to a boil then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook for 60 minutes.
Lay the fried aubergine slices over the top of the stew. Replace the lid and cook for a further 30 minutes until the lamb is fully tender and the aubergine has absorbed the sauce. Serve over rice.

attrs.solution: The aubergine needs to be properly fried before going into the stew. Ensure the oil is hot enough to seal the surface quickly. Add the aubergine only in the final 30 minutes.
Add a pinch of caster sugar to balance the tomatoes. The long cooking time also mellows acidity, so ensure the stew has had a full 90 minutes total.
Remove the lid for the final 15 minutes and increase to a steady simmer. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

content.text: Khoresh Bademjan is found in Iranian homes from Tehran to Shiraz. It is a summer dish in the traditional sense, tied to the aubergine season. The combination of lamb and aubergine goes back centuries in the Middle East. The saffron and tomato version is distinctly Persian. It is always served alongside steamed rice and a simple herb salad.
